videos.script: Lesson 2 answered with JSON. People do not read JSON. They read pages. {{pages}} Writing HTML inside Python strings is the mistake every web framework exists to prevent. Django's answer is the template. An HTML file with holes in it, which a view fills from a dictionary. {{template}} You write one base page with the header and the stylesheet. Every other page extends it, and fills in only what is different. {{inherit}} Then you type HTML into the search box on purpose. Django prints it back as text, not as a tag. That is escaping, and it is on by default. {{escape}} Then a form, to register for an event. A POST with no token is refused. A POST with the token is accepted, and answered with a redirect, so reloading the page never registers anyone twice. {{form}} You fill the twelve seats of a workshop, and watch the thirteenth person get turned away. {{full}} And you break templates in the four ways they break. Three of them shout. One of them prints nothing at all, and that is the one to watch for.
